issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect Stock to provide a public method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). The template Stock class declares a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead, while the solution implements addToStockIngredients. This method-name/signature mismatch can prevent students from following the specification or compiling code that calls addToStockIngredients as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock class match the specification and solution by renaming or adding a method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (public) that appends a StockIngredient to the stockIngredients array. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to reference addItem if that name is intended. Prefer renaming addItem to addToStockIngredients in the template to preserve the educational intent.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) names the method for adding a StockIngredient as addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), and the solution implements this exact name. However, the template Stock class exposes an addItem(StockIngredient) method instead. This mismatch (addItem vs addToStockIngredients) can confuse students mapping the UML/problem requirements to the provided template and the expected solution API, causing them to search for or implement the wrong method name when integrating SealSaloon and Stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the UML and solution: rename Stock.addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in the template (or provide a forwarder method addToStockIngredients that calls addItem). This ensures a consistent identifier across problem, template, and solution.
